inline_comments.comment: This override block for `*.md` and `*.mdx` is dead code. Both `*.md` (line 38) and `*.mdx` (line 39) are already listed in `ignorePatterns`, so oxfmt will never process those files and will never reach this override. The `importOrderSeparation`/`importOrderSortSpecifiers` options here have no effect. Either remove the override, or remove the patterns from `ignorePatterns` if formatting these files is actually desired in the future.

The `**/frameworks/angular/template/**/*.ts` glob in this override is unreachable because `code/frameworks/angular/template/**` is already excluded via `ignorePatterns` (line 33). Those files will never be formatted, so this half of the `files` array does nothing. The `**/frameworks/angular/src/**/*.ts` half is valid and should stay. Consider simplifying to just `["**/frameworks/angular/src/**/*.ts"]` to avoid confusion.

This line contains a real bug fix hidden among the indentation changes: `

    ` (an unclosed opening tag) was corrected to `

`. The old code left the `
    ` list element unclosed, producing malformed HTML in the error UI. Good catch — but since this is a semantic change rather than a purely mechanical format rewrite, it warrants a call-out in the PR description and ideally a standalone commit or note so it's not lost in the formatter noise.

The old `code/package.json` lint-staged ran bare `oxfmt` (which formats files in-place before committing). This new config runs `oxfmt --check` (validation only), which will fail the commit if any staged file is not already formatted. This is a notable developer-experience change: contributors now need to manually run `oxfmt` or `yarn fmt:write` before committing, or the pre-commit hook will reject their changes. If this shift to check-only is intentional, it should be documented (e.g., in a CONTRIBUTING guide or the PR description) so developers know to run `yarn fmt:write` first.

The `scripts/**/*.{...}` lint-staged pattern only runs `yarn --cwd scripts lint:js:cmd` — there is no `oxfmt --check` step here, unlike the `code/**` patterns above (lines 44–51) which both lint and check formatting. Files in `scripts/` can be committed with formatting violations that would be caught in CI but not pre-commit. This inconsistency seems unintentional given the goal of unifying formatting enforcement.

`cd .. && yarn fmt:check` in a package.json script is fragile. The `cd` relies on the shell's working directory being exactly `code/` when the script runs, which holds when invoked normally but can break with `yarn --cwd code lint` called from an unexpected location or on Windows. The idiomatic and portable alternative is `yarn --cwd .. fmt:check`, which does not depend on shell directory state.

The NX cache `inputs` still lists only `"{workspaceRoot}/docs/**/*"`, but the command (`yarn fmt:check` from `{workspaceRoot}`) now runs `oxfmt --check .` against the entire project — not just the docs directory. This means NX will serve a cached "pass" result even if a TypeScript file in `code/` was changed and is now mis-formatted, because that file is not part of the declared inputs. Either scope the command back to docs only, or expand `inputs` to include `["**/*"]` (or the relevant file globs) to match what the command actually checks.

The file is missing a trailing newline (`\ No newline at end of file`). Most editors and linters (including EditorConfig, which this project uses per `.vscode/extensions.json`) expect files to end with a newline. The same issue exists in `.vscode/extensions.json`. Ironically, the formatter being added here should enforce this — consider running `oxfmt` on these config files as part of this PR.

Missing trailing newline at end of file. See the same note on `.vscode/settings.json` — both VSCode config files should end with a newline to satisfy EditorConfig and standard Unix text-file conventions.

The old `docs:fmt:check` script included a helpful fallback message: `|| echo 'Please run "docs:fmt:write" in the "scripts" directory to fix the issues'`. The new `fmt:check` removes this hint. When CI fails on docs formatting, contributors now get a raw oxfmt error with no guidance on how to fix it. Consider preserving the hint: `oxfmt --check ./_snippets || (echo 'Run yarn fmt:write in scripts/ to fix formatting' && exit 1)`.

general_comments.comment: `"embeddedLanguageFormatting": "off"` is added to `.oxfmtrc.json` without any comment explaining why. This disables formatting of embedded languages (JS inside HTML, CSS inside JS template literals, etc.) and has broad effects. A short inline comment (or a note in the PR description) explaining the rationale — e.g., avoiding churn in styled-components template literals or preventing conflicts with Angular HTML templates — would help future contributors understand whether this option is safe to revisit.

The `$schema` in the new `.oxfmtrc.json` points to `"./node_modules/oxfmt/configuration_schema.json"`. This gives VSCode JSON IntelliSense for the config, which is great. One thing to verify: this path is relative to the file's location (the workspace root), so it will work correctly for editors opening the repo at root. If anyone opens a subdirectory (e.g., just `code/`) as a workspace, the schema reference will silently fail. This is a minor concern and a common trade-off with local `node_modules` schema references.
